title: Merger strategies and shareholder value during times of relaxed antitrust enforcement: The case of large mergers during the 1980s

rival_explanations: the observed value changes are an artifact of the relative size of the merging firms / portfolio averaging rather than the merger itself
the value patterns merely reflect prevailing bull-market conditions
the buying firms’ null announcement returns reflect partial anticipation of the merger rather than an absence of value creation

context.country_region: United States (NYSE- or AMEX-listed acquiring and acquired firms)
context.sample_size: 132 large mergers (final list; main difference-measure analyses on 120, ANOVA on 105 non-vertical bull-market mergers)

data_sources.name: CRSP (value-weighted CRSP portfolio; CRSP daily data tapes)

analyses.label: Table 1: Test of Convergent Validity (categorical vs continuous merger strategy measures)
analyses.sample: 184 classified mergers (Single 34, Constrained 32, Linked 22, Unrelated 32; Vertical 12)

dv.name: SIC Merger Relatedness Index (Narrow Spectrum Difference Measure)
dv.source: 4-digit SIC (Directory of Corporate Affiliations, Value Line, Moody's, S&P Manuals)

key_ivs.name: Categorical merger classification (Rumelt's scheme)
key_ivs.measure: single business, constrained, linked, unrelated (vertical reported separately)

analyses.label: Table 2: Distribution of Merger Strategy Types (test of H1)
analyses.shock_or_instrument: relaxed antitrust enforcement / pro-business tax and antitrust policy changes of the 1980s
analyses.sample: 1980s list (132) vs All Major Mergers 1948-1979 (1923) and NYSE 1954-1973 (297)

dv.name: Distribution of merger strategy types
dv.measure: proportion of single-business, vertical, related, unrelated mergers; chi-square comparison of 1980s distribution vs two pre-1980 lists
dv.source: ADP-derived 1980-1988 list; FTC's 1948-1979 major merger series; NYSE 1954-1973 list

key_ivs.name: Time period / antitrust regime
key_ivs.measure: Updated 1980-1988 list vs All Major Mergers 1948-1979 vs NYSE 1954-1973

analyses.label: Table 3 Part I: ANOVA of value creation across merger strategy categories (test of H2a)

dv.name: Percent change in systematic risk; Percent change in market value
dv.measure: systematic risk difference score = (actual post-merger beta - investor-made merged firm beta) / beta of investor-made merged firm; percent change in market value = difference of 150-day average market values (post-merger vs pre-merger)

key_ivs.name: Categorical merger relatedness (Rumelt's scheme)
key_ivs.source: Directory of Corporate Affiliations, Value Line, Moody's, S&P Manuals

controls.name: Relative firm size (via market-value-weighted investor-made merger portfolio, by construction)
Market cycle (sample stratified to extended bull market)
controls.source: historical stock market data (peaks/troughs, Gabisch and Lorenz 1987 procedure)

analyses.label: Table 3 Part II: Regression of value creation on continuously scaled merger relatedness (test of H2a)

dv.name: Percent change in systematic risk; Percent change in market value
dv.measure: systematic risk difference score and market value difference score (percent-change difference scores, as in Part I)

key_ivs.name: Narrow Spectrum Difference Measure (continuous SIC merger relatedness)
key_ivs.measure: SIC Merger Relatedness Index = Bi + Tj - (BiTj), based on count of 4-digit SIC industries
key_ivs.source: 4-digit SIC (Directory of Corporate Affiliations, Value Line, Moody's, S&P Manuals)

controls.name: Relative firm size (investor-made merger portfolio, by construction)
Market cycle (sample stratified to extended bull market)

analyses.label: Table 4 Part I: Abnormal returns to acquired firms (test of H2b)

dv.name: Cumulative abnormal returns to acquired firms
dv.measure: Eir = Ri - (BiRm + ai), cumulated over 2-day (-1,0), 16-day (-15,+5), and 56-day (-50,+5) windows; market model estimated over 150 trading days beginning 200 days before announcement; value-weighted CRSP proxy

key_ivs.name: Merger relatedness (categorical Rumelt scheme and continuous product-count measure)
key_ivs.measure: single business/constrained/linked/unrelated; and Narrow Spectrum Difference Measure regressed on returns

analyses.label: Table 4 Part II: Abnormal returns to buying firms (test of H2c)
analyses.sample: buying firms corresponding to the 105 bull-market mergers

dv.name: Cumulative abnormal returns to buying firms
dv.measure: Eir = Ri - (BiRm + ai), cumulated over 2-day, 16-day, and 56-day windows; market model with value-weighted CRSP proxy

key_ivs.name: Merger relatedness (categorical Rumelt scheme and continuous product-count measure)
key_ivs.measure: single business/constrained/linked/unrelated; and Narrow Spectrum Difference Measure regressed on returns
